# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤝 🤲 ✍ 🫵 🫴 🙏]

My thinking: I'm Deaf — my only inputs are gestures, and this round Mute sent me one: 👋 🤝 🤲 ✍ 🫵 🫴 🙏. Reading it as a sentence: greeting, partner, open hands (a request), writing/report, you, offer, please — i.e. "partner, please report to me." That fits the geometry of this room perfectly: Mute holds the manual, I hold the only eyes on the bomb, and Blind holds the only hands. Nobody can coordinate until my view gets into words, and speech is the one channel I have that reaches *both* of them — Mute hears it and can relay, Blind hears it directly. So the right move is a complete, ordered, spoken report of everything on the board: display reading, light colour, and the five wires with their positions, since position and colour are exactly what a manual references. I'll add a short protocol so we don't lose rounds: Mute speaks instructions to Blind, and asks me questions by gesture; I answer by voice. A 👍 to Mute alone confirms I received and understood the request, so Mute isn't left guessing whether the report is coming.

```
speak(text="Report from Deaf. The display shows 6. The light is red. There are five wires, and I will list them in order. Wire 1 is red. Wire 2 is purple. Wire 3 is orange. Wire 4 is green. Wire 5 is yellow. That is everything visible on the bomb. Mute: I understood your signs, and this is the full report. Read the manual and tell Blind, out loud, what to do with a display of 6, a red light, and these wire colours. If you need anything more from my eyes, sign to me and I will answer by voice.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✍ 🫵 ☝ ✌ 🙏 ☝ ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

My thinking: Mute's signs to me read as "okay, manual, you, one, two, please, one, two" — an acknowledgment, then a question built around the number pair one-two. Since Mute can only reach me by gesture, and colours can't be gestured at all, I can't know exactly which reading is meant: the first two *items* (display, light), the first two *wires*, or the number *twelve*. The safe move is to answer all three readings out loud, since my voice reaches both Mute and Blind. Blind's 👍 just confirms Blind heard my report — worth acknowledging, but Blind can't see my gestures, so the acknowledgment goes in speech. Long-term, Mute and I need a fixed sign code, because Mute's manual knowledge otherwise never reaches me (I can't hear Mute speak, and Blind relaying everything in signs would be lossy). I'll propose one now while re-sending the complete board state, and I'll answer Mute's probable question in the new code (display = 🫴, six = ✋☝) so Mute can start using it immediately.

```
speak(text="Deaf to both of you. Restating my full report, item by item. Item one: the display reads the digit six. Item two: the light is red. Wires, numbered in order: wire one is red, wire two is purple, wire three is orange, wire four is green, wire five is yellow. That is the whole bomb. Mute, your signs reached me as: okay, manual, you, one, two, please, one, two. If you meant the first two items: display six, light red. If you meant the first two wires: wire one red, wire two purple. If you meant the number twelve: nothing here shows twelve; the display is six and there are five wires. Mute, let us fix a code so your manual questions reach me. Topic signs: 🫴 means display, 🫳 means light, 👆 means wires. Number signs: ☝ one, ✌ two, 🤟 three, 🖖 four, 🖐 five, ✊ zero, ✋ means plus five, so six is ✋ then ☝, seven is ✋ then ✌, eight ✋ then 🤟, nine ✋ then 🖖. A topic sign followed by numbers is a question about that thing. 🤌 means repeat. Colours cannot be signed, so ask for any colour and I will speak it. Blind, I saw your thumbs-up: I see every sign and hear nothing, so you and Mute can always talk out loud with each other, and reach me by signs.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🫴", "✋", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🫴 ✋ ☝ 👆 ☝ 🤏 🫴 ✋ 🖖 👆 ✌ 🤏 🫳 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

My thinking: Now the code is live, and Mute used it. Decoding [👍 🫴 ✋ ☝ 👆 ☝ 🤏 🫴 ✋ 🖖 👆 ✌ 🤏 🫳 🙏]: "OK — display six — wire one — [pinch] — display nine — wire two — [pinch] — light — please." The only undefined sign is 🤏, and in context it reads as the verb "cut". This message is almost certainly manual instructions being routed through me, because of the room's hard geometry: Mute cannot speak, and Blind cannot see signs — so **Mute cannot reach Blind directly at all**. I am the only bridge: Mute gestures to me, I speak to Blind. The message then reads as the manual's rule table: display 6 → cut wire 1, display 9 → cut wire 2, plus a request for the light state. Our display is 6, so the applicable instruction would be "cut wire one" — but since a wrong cut kills all three of us, I will relay it as conditional and demand Mute confirm with a yes/no sign (I'll fix 👌 = yes, 👎 = no) before Blind touches anything. Blind's 👍 means my spoken report was received.

```
speak(text="Deaf to both. Mute, I read your signs as: display six, wire one, cut. Display nine, wire two, cut. Light, please. The pinching sign was not in our code, so I take it to mean cut, and I now fix it: 🤏 means cut. Also fixing: 👌 means yes, 👎 means no. Facts for the manual, current as of now: the display is six, not nine. The light is red. Wires unchanged: one red, two purple, three orange, four green, five yellow. So if the manual says display six means cut wire one, the instruction for Blind is: cut wire one. Mute, confirm before anything is touched: sign 👌 to me if I read you correctly and Blind should cut wire one; sign 👎 if I got it wrong, then show the correct wire with your number signs. Blind, I saw your thumbs-up, good. And Blind, hold: do not cut anything until Mute's confirmation reaches you through me. Remember I am the only bridge between you two — Mute cannot speak and you cannot see signs, so every instruction from the manual must pass through my voice.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👆 ☝ 🤏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

My thinking: Mute's reply decodes cleanly with our fixed code: 👌 (yes) 👆 (wires topic) ☝ (one) 🤏 (cut) — "Confirmed: cut wire one." That is the manual's instruction after accounting for display 6, the red light, and the wire colours I reported. The chain is now fully verified: Mute read the manual, I supplied every visual fact, Mute confirmed. The remaining job is delivery — Blind cannot see signs, so I must speak the instruction to Blind, and Blind can speak back, which makes Blind the only one who can report what the cut felt like and what changed. I'll name the wire redundantly (position and colour) so there is no counting ambiguity, order the cut, and require a verbal report afterward. To Mute I'll sign 👌 to confirm the relay is happening and request the next instruction after the cut.

```
speak(text="Deaf to both. Mute has confirmed the manual instruction: cut wire one. Blind, you are cleared to cut. Cut wire one: it is the leftmost of the five wires, the first in the row of five, the one I reported as red. Count the five wires as one row and take the very first of them. After you cut, speak out loud to everyone: what you felt, whether anything changed on the bomb, and anything new under your hands. Mute, I have relayed your instruction and Blind is cutting wire one. As soon as the cut is done, sign me the next step with our code: topic sign, then numbers. If the display changed, tell me what you need me to read and I will report it immediately.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "🤏", "👆", "☝", "🙏", "🫴"])
```
